utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are today having a videolink for the next witness to appear. I first wanted to establish in view of what I see on my screen that both video and audio are functioning well. Could the representative of the Registry in Pristina inform me whether the audio and video function is okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Good morning, Mr. President. We see the courtroom and we can hear in English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before -- excuse me. Your Honour, just before we begin I wonder if I might raise the question of timing for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I note from e-mail correspondence yesterday afternoon that the Prosecution have decided not to elicit the testimony of this witness pursuant to Rule 92 ter. I'm anxious that the time left available to us before the normal time for ceasing today may place all parties under some pressure if the Prosecution were to elicit the testimony orally in full, unless it's to be done in a truncated form. I wonder if we might raise the issue now to save it arising in a concertina'd form in the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the message from the Chamber, Mr. Di Fazio, was that in view of the time -- of course you are free to choose the way of presenting the evidence as you wish but it is the last day before the recess that you are limited to the time that you indicated. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if the Trial Chamber takes the view that you would prefer me to use the provisions of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I leave it up to you. The message is quite clear that you should stay within the time-limits. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, perhaps to accommodate you, if you would be fully unable to manage within the time and the time you indicated would be one hour? MR. DI FAZIO: I expect ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, the time scheduled was for one hour, is that -- MR. DI FAZIO: I believe so, if Your Honours please, yes. And I think I can deal with that in that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would run into great problems, the Chamber would consider upon a request, and after having heard how you used your time, to consider an additional 15 minutes but not at the expense of Defence time. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I understand that, if Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, perhaps -- usually we take the same time for cross as for examination-in-chief. That would limit you to one hour respectively, one hour and 15 minutes for all Defence teams. Would that do?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is some pressure of time but we will make it do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Di Fazio, I do understand that there are no applications for protective measures for the next witness to appear -- MR. DI FAZIO: No, there is none from the Prosecution, as I stand here, but of course I think the Trial Chamber is aware of the notification that I provided to the Trial Chamber concerning certain information that the Prosecution had received from VWS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I suggest to the parties -- I take it that Defence counsel have also received this information, that is, where the Prosecution has not applied for protective measures, that nevertheless there might be a protection issue, which I would prefer to deal with in private session to start with. Therefore, I would like to turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Registrar in Pristina. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stijovic. You'll first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, it's important that you answer my questions as simply as possible so that we can deal with your evidence quickly this morning and not delay you for any longer than is necessary. It's in your interests and in the interests of all the parties in this courtroom that we get through it fast. So bear that in mind. If you can answer a question with a yes or no, please do so. I want to put some personal details, and can you tell us if these details are correct. Born in Kosovo, in the village of Pozar, in the municipality of Decani, and you lived there until 1998, and in particular your date of birth is the 10th of February, 1966; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Your father was a gentleman named Kostadin and your mother's name was Rosanda. You have three brothers and three sisters; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, what your occupation was in April of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Di Fazio. Is your first name Novak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, what your occupation was in April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I was a worker, an employee at the factory of pumps in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what specifically was your occupation? What type of work did you do?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in the security detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know two brothers named Stojanovic -- surname Stojanovic, Mijat and Dragoslav?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know an individual named Veselin Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I know him, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What relation -- is Veselin Stijovic any relation to you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is a relation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What is the relationship?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: A relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. What sort of relative? Uncle? Aunt? Cousin? Grandfather? What sort of relationship?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: He is my cousin, my uncle's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in -- in 1998, did anything happen to those three individuals that you became aware of?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what occurred to them and, importantly, tell the Trial Chamber, please, how you know what happened to them; in other words, your source of information.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I learned this from their mother, who was at Decani. She was put up at a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And what precisely did you learn? You said you learnt this. Now, what did you learn? What was reported to you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I was told that they were at their house in Dubrava village and they were caught by the so-called KLA army. The KLA took them to Glodjane village, to the KLA headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did you --

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: That they mistreated them and beat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever lay eyes on either Veselin or the two Stojanovic brothers after this episode?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I saw Veselin and Mijat but not Dragoslav because Dragoslav was transferred to a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: At the time did either of those two men have any apparent injuries?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Briefly tell the Trial Chamber which of the men had injuries, if it was only one; and secondly, what sort of injuries you observed.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Both of them had injuries, and visible injuries all over their bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want you to turn now to another topic, and that is the question of your work. You've told us about your job. In April of 1998, did you commute to your work from Pozar?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: From work I went back home to Pozar village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was that on a day-to-day basis or did you sometimes stay in town after your work?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I would stay on in town for two or three hours after work when I was not pressed to get home early.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And -- and in April of 1998 were you doing or working day shifts or night shifts?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: You mean on that day? MR. DI FAZIO: It's not in dispute I think, if Your Honours please, that an episode occurred to this man where he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm referring to the day on which you were beaten. Now, on the night preceding had you been attacked -- sorry, had you been working on night shift or day shift?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I was working on the night shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. You've mentioned that day. Can you remember the day that -- the date on which the events we're about to talk about happened, the actual date?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was the date?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: 21st of April, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a gentleman named Stanisa Radosevic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And do you know his mother; and if so, what's her name?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I know his mother; her name is Rosanda.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see those two people, Stanisa and his mother, Rosanda, on the 21st of April, 1998?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where did you see them and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I saw them at Decani. We met there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you go anywhere with them?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Please tell the Trial Chamber where you -- where you left for.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: We went home from Decani towards Pozar village, and Stanisa and Rosa went to their home, to Dasinovac village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did that journey to your respective homes involve you travelling together or separately?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: We went together, but in two cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was travelling in the car -- in which car?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I was riding in my car and Stanisa and his mother were in their own car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And I don't think anyone's going to mind if I lead you on this. Your car was a red Yugo and the Radosevics were travelling in a grey Lada; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, did anything happen to this party of which you were a member on your homeward journey?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: When we got to Pozar village, we were stopped by KLA soldiers. They were suddenly in front of us with their guns trained at us, so we had to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber -- comment on these issues: Were the men armed?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] [Indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, we still can see you, but we'll wait until you give us a signal that the video connection is restored.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Di Fazio, you are asking if they were armed, but that was already mentioned -- MR. DI FAZIO: It was. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: If you could ask in a more specific way -- MR. DI FAZIO: As I was going over the transcript, I realised that was a pointless question so I won't ask that. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, has the -- in Pristina, has the reason for the interruption been detected and is there any expectation as far as the time is concerned it would need to re-establish the videolink?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] We have been communicating with the technicians in The Hague and they are working on that. It is something that has to be fixed from The Hague. We still receive sounds, but the image is still not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber understands that the line has to be disconnected, then to wait for two minutes, and then to try to re-establish it. So therefore, some patience might be needed. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, just on a matter that doesn't require video connection but may be important -- I don't think it would be important but I just want to alert you and the Defence. We've asked that a copy of the statement be faxed down -- faxed, faxed, down to the place where the witness is in case it becomes necessary. And we hope that our investigator will be able to provide a copy to the -- to the Registry official in the event that it's needed because it's not available down there in e-court. So that's -- if Defence counsel see the registry official being handed documents by an investigator, it's merely that and merely as a matter of insurance, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. The last couple of minutes the only thing that happened is that the Chamber hears some music. In musical terms, I would say, the Chamber would like to have it "da capo al fine." That is, let's start again and let's keep up until the very end. Madam Registrar, is there any -- I mean, the two minutes are, by and large, over now. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar in Pristina, can you now see us and hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Yes, Your Honour, we can see and hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I was asking you about this roadblock that you encountered in, I think you said, Pozar. You've told us there were armed men. Can you describe if they were uniformed and whether the uniforms bore any insignia?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Some of them were in uniforms, some were in civilian clothes. Those that were in uniforms had the UCK, KLA, insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you recognise any of the individuals amongst the men who stopped you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell us their names, please?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember all of them. I only remember that Kujtim Berisha was there as well as Jusuf, whose last name I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. The gentleman Kujtim Berisha, what -- can you tell us anything about his background, what his job was, for instance?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: He is from the same village, from Pozar. I don't know what he was doing at the time. I do know that he used to be a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you happen to know what his ethnicity was?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he's an Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Following this stop at this roadblock, did you continue onwards?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: We did continue onwards, but not towards our home, but towards Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did you go via Rznic and did you stop in Rznic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: We did go through Rznic, but we did not stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were there any KLA soldiers in Rznic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Uniformed and armed, as they had been at Pozar, or not?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were armed and they wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there a roadblock of any sort in Rznic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And from there, were you eventually taken to Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And was that in both cars that you described before, the grey Lada and the red Yugo?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And were you guarded with KLA soldiers whilst you were travelling in the car or cars?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I just want you now, please, to go back to Pozar. There's just one other matter that I need to ask you about that. Were you -- when you were in Pozar, were you asked by the KLA soldiers anything about yourselves or your intentions?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They only asked us where we were going. We said that we were bound for home. Then they told us that we could not go home, that we had no business there anymore. And so from that point they took us to Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. All right. Let's turn your mind back now to -- turn your mind back to Glodjane, please. Just for the sake of completeness, the situation now is that you've arrived in your -- in the Lada and the Yugo. Stanisa is there with his mother, Rosanda, and yourself; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were there any KLA soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: About how many? Were they all armed and uniformed?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact number. There may have been between 30 and 50 of them, I'm not sure. Most of them were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you and Stanisa?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, something did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Now I'd like you to tell the Trial Chamber in your own words, please, what happened to you and Stanisa.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived at Glodjane, the minute we got out of the car they started beating us. They hit us with rods. They kicked us. They punched us with their fists. They hit us with rifle-butts. And this lasted for some time. I cannot recall with precision how long, perhaps some 20 minutes or half an hour. I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And can you tell us if when you were being attacked in this way whether they -- any words were uttered by the men who were attacking you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, words were uttered, but I'm in fact unable to remember everything that they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you remember -- let me ask you this: Were you questioned by the men?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you insulted, verbally, I mean?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: What worse insult can you have than being beaten?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm interested in anything that they might have -- I'm not asking about any questioning that might have occurred, I'm interested in any insults or anything they might have said to you whilst the beating was going on apart from questions.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, I'm not sure. Perhaps they swore at us, but I cannot remember that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Now, what about the questioning. Can you tell us what you were asked about?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They asked us mostly about the police forces, where they were, how many of them there were. They asked about the head of the police in Decani, about the commander of the police station in Rznic, and possibly also inquired after some other people. I cannot recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You said at Pozar you were told there was nothing for you anymore in your village or words to that effect. Was anything similar said to you on this occasion in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the same thing as in Pozar, that there was nothing for us at home, that there was nothing for us there anymore, and that we should up and leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there any suggestion as to where you should go?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: To Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. During the course of the assault that you suffered, did you lose consciousness or did Stanisa lose consciousness, either of you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I did not, and I believe that Stanisa did faint for a short moment at a certain point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And during this time that both you men were being beaten, was Rosanda, the mother, was she untouched?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, she wasn't touched. She wasn't touched.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Stanisa eventually leave the scene?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Just perhaps before I ask him about that I should ask you this: Was there any blood on you or on Stanisa that you saw?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: There was blood on Stanisa and there wasn't any on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was he bleeding from, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It was from the back of his head, I believe. I believe that that was where he sustained a hit with a rifle-butt.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, you told us that Stanisa was -- eventually left the scene. Was that to go off and collect some rifles?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell the Trial Chamber -- thank you. Tell the Trial Chamber, please, how that came about, how that was negotiated. What happened such that he left the scene?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They asked us whether we had any weapons. Stanisa said that he had a hunting rifle and that I also had one, so that the two of us had hunting rifles. Then they asked us who would go and get those hunting rifles. We couldn't make up our minds so they chose to send Stanisa to get them, and he went home to get those rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what happened at that point to you and the mother, Rosanda?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we remained at Glodjane. They locked us up in a small room, in a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how long were you there for?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: You mean how long we were locked up?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That's right, in the room. How long?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour or an hour and a half. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: During that time did you hear any voices?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did you hear and whose voice did you hear?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I heard my father's voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you provide a little more detail, if you can, please. How did it sound? Was it clear enough to hear? Could you hear what he was saying?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I think that I heard him say, "Don't throw -- knock off my cap." Probably someone had hit him and knocked off his cap from his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Are they the only words -- specific words that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard just that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you were in the room for a period of time. How did you come to leave the room and what happened at that point?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, in fact, how we came to leave that room and what happened. I'm unable to exactly describe that. Simply, one -- a man came and he told us, You can go, and we went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You -- you and the mother, Rosanda. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Stanisa's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: We went out in the street. We asked them where we should go, and then someone said, "Go wherever you please." We went to the village of Prilep, which is on the Decani-Djakovica road, and then headed towards Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Just a bit more detail, please. How did you get from Glodjane to Prilep and why Prilep? Why not back to Pozar or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know why we would go back to Pozar because here on this road, the one to Prilep, this was a busy road, and we hoped that someone would come by and give us a ride to Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: It may be clear in your mind, but I'd like to be absolutely clear about this. You said you lived in Pozar. When you said -- when they said to you, You're free to go wherever you want, why not go to Pozar? That's my question. Now, it may be obvious to you but I want to hear it from you in clear detail. Why not go back to Pozar, your home?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They would not allow us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is that something that was said to you or is that something you thought was absolutely clear from the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They said so. They did say so. They said, "You can go wherever you please, but you cannot go home."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I ask: What do you mean by "go"? What happened to the cars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stanisa left in his car and he did not return. My car was there at Glodjane, but I couldn't start it. I couldn't start the engine. So that some of them towed us to the village of Prilep, me and Stanisa's mother, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In Stanisa's car? That was -- which car were you towed?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: In my red Yugo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks, thanks, that's clear. Did you eventually make it to the main road between Decani and Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That's what I'd like to know. I'd like to know a little bit more about that last -- very last part of your trip. How did you actually get the vehicle to that point, to the main road that runs between Decani and Djakovica? Was it towed? Did you push it? How did you physically get it there?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: The car was towed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. And was that car being towed by KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who made the decision to stop the towing once you hit the main road?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They made that decision. They simply towed us there to the main road and they left us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why you wouldn't -- they wouldn't tow you any further?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Just do the best you can. Approximately how many kilometres would you say it is to be towed from Glodjane to the main road that runs between Decani and Djakovica, how many kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: That is about 7 or 8 kilometres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. And I think that eventually a Serb policeman found you and you made your way eventually to -- to Decani; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm now drawing to an end of my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You've told us this morning about some comments that were made to you about going back to Serbia and not being able to go back to your home or go to your home. When those words were being said to you, what language was being used? Were they speaking to you in Albanian or Serbian?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: In Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you speak any Albanian or understand at least any Albanian?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: A little, to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And just go back to the -- what you told us about Stanisa Radosevic going off to get the rifles. Did anyone give him anything just before he set off on that trip to go and collect the rifles?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It was an emblem of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of that, as far as you could ascertain?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Something like a pass, like a laissez-passer to help him get home and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. And just -- just turn your mind back to the trip that you told us about. You told us you were stopped at a check-point which was in Pozar and you also mentioned a check-point in Rznic. Now, at that time were you travelling through Rznic on a regular basis, I mean in the days before the 21st of April, 1998?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't go regularly when I had an errand to run, but I do go rather often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there a police station in Rznic at the time?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Not at that time. I don't think so, not on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's be specific about that. What day are you talking about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, before we continue it seems that we have a video problem now on our side. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you still need? MR. DI FAZIO: Five or six minutes. Apologies. Five to six minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it would be best then to have a break now and you then continue your examination-in-chief -- a break would be -- well, let's say until ten minutes past 12.00. Then you would finish your examination-in-chief 20 minutes past 12.00, which would allow for considerably more time for cross-examination. I suggest that we have the break now and have the-- MR. DI FAZIO: That's perfectly fine by me, as the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar in Pristina, we can't see you clearly; therefore, the Chamber decides to have the break now, to resume in 25 minutes from now, that's ten minutes past 12.00, in the hope that the videolink is functioning again in all respects. We have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment I see no connection with Pristina, but now it appears on the screen again. Madam Registrar, in Pristina, can you hear us? Can you see us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Yes, we do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can hear and see you. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Stijovic, for answering the questions so succinctly and briefly. Please continue and we'll finish shortly. You said -- I was asking you before the break after the 21st of April, the day that all of these events happened to you. On that day do you know if there was a police station in Rznic operating or not?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You've described in your evidence today check-points that you encountered at Pozar and Rznic. Did you on your way to Glodjane go through a place called Kodralija?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were there any check-points in Kodralija?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, there were no check-points, but there was soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And just to wrap-up on that. Were they KLA soldiers --

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, there were more civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Oh, I see. All right. Thank you very much. Did your father report to you what had happened to him on that day; and if he did, can you tell us what the -- what he told you had happened to him?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing happened to him except that this man, I don't know who, hit him and knocked the cap off his head, nothing but that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he provide you with any information as to how he got there?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: He said that they stopped him, like us, in the same village, Pozar, at that check-point; and from there, they took him to Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know or did he report to you if he had been driving a vehicle or whether he was walking at the time that he was stopped?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: He was on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. And the place that you were taken to and the place at which you heard your father's voice from another room, what place exactly was that?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It was at the entrance to Glodjane village, looking from Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did the -- did the building or place that you were taken to, the room, did it have anything to do with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It looked to me like a private house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you have any information about any KLA headquarters in Glodjane? I'm not suggesting there was one. I'm just asking you: Do you have any information about such a place?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there. I haven't been there, but I heard that there was headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Following this episode on the 21st of April in which you were attacked and beaten, did you suffer any injuries; and if so, what were they?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did sustain some injuries, although I didn't feel them in the first days. But later on I started having problems with my spine and I still suffer from that today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: About how long after the injury did -- sorry, the episode I should say, did you start to have these problems with your spine?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Maybe three, four, maybe even five months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Had you ever suffered from such problems before the episode on the 21st of April?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you beaten -- you've told us you were beaten, but were you beaten on your back on the 21st of April?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You are a Serb by ethnicity, are you not?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Just answer my next question with a yes or no. In April of 1998 did you know or did you know of Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I had heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was his position at that time, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what he was at that time, but I learned later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When did you learn later and what did you learn later and from whom did you learn later anything about him?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Just a couple of days later, maybe four, five, days later or a week, I learnt that he was the commander of the so-called KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And from whom did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the stories went around. I can't recall now who told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What reputation did he have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I object to that question. I think we've pushed this absolutely to its limits with Mr. Di Fazio has already elicited the content of stories which went around that the witness cannot recall the source of. With respect, further general questioning of that kind in our submission is entirely inappropriate and not likely in any way to assist the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: That depends entirely on what he heard and how he heard and the sources of his information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is granted. Mr. Di Fazio, apart from that, the five to six minutes seem to become already a bit more. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stijovic, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honour, I understand that it's unlikely that other counsel will have much, if anything, for this witness just to give Your Honour an indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I don't have to get nervous?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, I want to ask you some questions about the background to this sequence of events. You've told us that at various points you were being asked questions about the police in the area and where they were deployed, and I want to ask you some background questions in relation to that, if I may. When this event occurred, were you personally aware of the incidents which had taken place in Drenica at the end of February and the beginning of March? And I'm referring here to the incidents at Likoshan and Prekaze concerning the Ahmeti and Jashari families, in which more than 70 Albanians were killed at close range, including women, children, and the elderly. Were you aware of that background?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you had heard nothing about these incidents at that time. Is that your testimony, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to suggest to you that everybody in western Kosovo knew about these incidents because they were notorious massacres, as they were being described at the time.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe I had heard something, but I can't recall it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the Albanian --

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that I was aware of it when I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to suggest to you that the Albanian population in general in western Kosovo was frightened of that type of action taking place in the Dukagjin region?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not hear any answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You made some reference in your statement to heightened tensions, and I want to suggest to you that you knew that one of the reasons for heightened tension was that the Albanian civilian population were scared of massacres like Likoshan and Prekaze happening in Dukagjin.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were afraid, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So are you accepting that the Albanian population had a level of fear arising out of those incidents, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't think they had any reason to be frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You do know about the incident on the 24th of March in Gllogjan, don't you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you know about the fact that a policeman called Otovic died in that confrontation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think another policeman who has the same name as your brother, Momo Stijovic, was injured in that incident. Did you know about him?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember him having been there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know another police officer called Momo Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: A distant relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you knew, didn't you, that there had been a major operation by the paramilitary police in Gllogjan on that day?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you not know that three teenagers had been killed?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That wasn't you'd heard at all?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Had you heard that police had fired mortars at the houses of civilians in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I only heard the explosions, but I don't know what it was all about because it was far from my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You did hear the explosions on the day. Can you help us, were you aware that rockets were being fired from helicopters?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us about this, Mr. Stijovic. Did you know that the civilian population of Gllogjan fled the village in fear and that the village was evacuated for several days after the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact day when they left, but I know they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This was a major assault and you knew that, didn't you, Mr. Stijovic, a major military assault on that village?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Why did you think the villagers had left Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Because we were not safe down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Albanian population of Gllogjan, Mr. Stijovic, is what I'm referring to. The Albanian population of Gllogjan evacuated in consequence of this military operation, did they not?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You knew some of the police officers who took part in that operation personally, did you not?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which ones you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, a man called Drasko Vukicevic, you knew him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did he take part in the operation on the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was there the day Otovic was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you discuss the operation with him?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He was a neighbour of yours, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you were close friends of the Stojanovic brothers, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Predrag Stojanovic or Dragan, as he is sometimes called, he took part in that operation on the 24th of March, as well, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know Dragan that well. I really knew only the younger two brothers, Dragoslav and Mijat and I was closest to Vlado. I didn't know Dragan that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know, yes or no, whether Dragan had taken part in the operation on the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, I want to suggest to you that it was after this sequence of incidents, first Likoshan, then Prekaze, then Gllogjan on the 24th of March, it was after that sequence of attacks that the local Albanian population in the area around where you lived began to appear armed in the streets and started to organise vehicle checks and dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the group which stopped you in Pozhare, I just want to be clear about this, when you were first stopped and questioned in Pozhare, were that group, in fact, all in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Not all of them. There was some in civilian clothes but there was some in uniform as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember being interviewed a few days after this incident on the 25th of April in a cafe by a woman from a non-governmental humanitarian organisation?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I think so. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to suggest to you that you told her that the people who stopped you were armed civilians and that you saw other groups of armed civilians along the road from Pozhare to Irzniq, and that it was not until you got past Irzniq that you began to see men in uniforms. Now, first of all, is it possible that you said that to her?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I'd said that there were both civilians and soldiers in Pozar, whereas on the road towards Pozar to Rznic in Kodralija village and in the very centre of Rznic there was civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the civilians that you saw, they were armed as well, were they?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were they milling around with weapons, not doing anything in particular but simply standing by the side of the road?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if we could go very briefly into private session, please, and if the registry representative could take the bundle of documents that are in front of her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. This photograph just shown to the witness still needs a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In terms of a document number. I think in the light of the witness's answer, it probably doesn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, his testimony now is not understandable who is not who.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So to that extent I think it's preferable to have it in evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But under seal --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- MR. DI FAZIO: I would not -- respectfully agree with what Your Honour has just said, and in the Prosecution view it should go into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, the paragraph shown in the bundle which is ID52/0001 receives number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be D150, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in the view of the absence of any objection admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions now about Stanisa Radosevic. Are you still in touch with one another?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see him very often, just occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know that he's given evidence in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you hear it from him or from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Not from him, somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Have you seen him or spoken to him since he gave evidence?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you, if I may, please, in the light of that answer, about one or two aspects of the evidence that he gave us. First of all, he told us that the location where you were assaulted was about 2 or 300 metres outside Gllogjan on the Irzniq side of the road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said it was at the very entry point to Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, how are you defining the entry point to Gllogjan, by the first house or in some other way?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not exactly the first house. There were several houses on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic's evidence was that the reason why you ended up where you did was because your car broke down at that point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: My car broke down in Glodjane, but it had driven to Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, let me make my question clearer to you, Mr. Stijovic. What Mr. Radosevic told the Trial Chamber was that the reason why you got out of the vehicles where you did was because your car broke down on the way into Gllogjan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly, possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the house that you eventually went into was just the nearest house by the side of the road to where your car had broken down. Again, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the men who were involved in the assault upon you, these were people who gathered around after your car broke down, were they not?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were already there. I wasn't driving my own car. Jusuf was driving. I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whether you were driving or not, Mr. Stijovic, the question I'm asking to you -- asking you about is whether it was a matter of chance that that is where the vehicle came to stop.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't even aware that the car had broke down.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic has described the way in which the people at Pozhare, and then later those who were around you on the road into Gllogjan, were behaving. And I wanted to ask you one or two questions about that. He described it on both occasions as a scene in which no one seemed to be in charge. Is that a description with which you would agree?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, nobody was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It was a pretty chaotic scene with people arguing amongst themselves about what to do. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't notice them arguing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there quite a period of time that you were at Pozhare where no one could quite decide what to do next?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A short a period as that or was it considerably longer?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Perhaps five to ten minutes at most.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you agree, do you, that it was not clear to you at any stage whether anyone was in charge, either at Pozhare or during the initial period on the road into Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It was clear to me in Pozar but not in Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You've told us that you were being asked questions about the locations of the police. Were you also being asked questions about whether you, that is, yourself and Mr. Radosevic, or members of your family or people from your village were involved with the police?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't ask anything about me because they knew both me and my family, so they didn't need to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to read to you a passage from the record of the interview you gave to the lady from the humanitarian organisation and see if you agree with what she records you as having said, and I'll quote it to you. "They asked me if we had relatives on the police force, to which we said we didn't. They asked --"

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You agree with that proposition, do you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "They asked if any of the villagers was a member of the police force. We said none except for one they knew about already." Is that the kind of question that they were asking you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Radosevic has told us in his evidence that in addition to that, some people were asking which police officers had been responsible for shooting at Albanians on the 24th of March. Do you remember those questions being asked?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you just a few questions, please, about local Serb membership of the police and security services. First of all, you yourself were personally related, were you not, to Zoran Stijovic, a high-ranking official in the RDB, the State Security Service. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And quite a lot of your close friends, Mr. Stijovic, were involved in the paramilitary police during the conflict. Is that not right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Not many. A few of them perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you give us, please, the names of those you know who were involved in the paramilitary police at any stage during the conflict in Kosovo from amongst your friends?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Zoran Stijovic was the only one, but he worked in Pristina as far as I remember. So we didn't meet often and we were not that much in touch. As for the others, I don't know who might have been involved. Maybe only that neighbour Vukicevic. I can't think of anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we have it clear, Mr. Stijovic, when I use the term "paramilitary police," I am referring to the PJP, Posebne Jedinice Policije. You understand that expression, do you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it your evidence then that none of your other friends were members of the PJP at any point?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if I could ask Madam Registrar just to turn behind tab 3 in this file --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where, Mr. Stijovic, you'll see a list of names of individuals who were registered either as being on the payroll or as being issued weapons as members of the PJP -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, is this -- I understand that this is a document created by the Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, all of the supporting documents follow in tabs 4, 5, 6 -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yeah, I understand that. I have no problem with that. But document 3 is a list created by the Defence, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. I think that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, shouldn't the witness be informed of that. It is being presented to him as a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's being presented to him as a list of names of people who were registered, which is exactly what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps we could add that it's extracted from other documents so that the witness knows that this is not a kind of an original document -- MR. DI FAZIO: That's exactly what I mean. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can trace all the original documents, Mr. Stijovic, if we need to because they're also in this file, but what you see in front of you is a list of individuals who are and were registered as PJP members. Now, I want to go through the list with you and ask you which of them you knew or knew well. First, Rade Vlahovic was somebody you knew, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you not know he was a member of the PJP, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I know that he worked for the police; and as to his being a member of the PJP, I didn't know that. He worked in Djakovica it seems to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Stanisa Radosevic, the gentleman who you've been described being with on the occasion that you've told us about in April. Did you not know that he was employed by the PJP during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about during the conflict. I know that he joined the police later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'll come to that in a moment, if I may. Do you know Slobodan Markovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know Momcilo Markovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know Danilo Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I know one Danilo Stijovic, and this is an elderly man. In fact, he was deceased by then so I don't know whom exactly you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. You told us you know Predrag Stojanovic, although not as well as you know his brothers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, not as well as them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know anybody called Veselin Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Just slightly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Ljubisa Radunovic, someone I think you knew quite well. Is that correct, Ljubisa?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to --

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It's Ljubisa Radunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want, if I may, then to ask you about another individual, a man called Zvonko Markovic, a cousin, I believe, of the Vlahovics. You know him as well. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He was a friend of yours, was he not?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were not -- we are not close.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic has given evidence before this Tribunal that Stanisa Radosevic was a police officer during 1998. I just want to be clear about this, Mr. Stijovic. Is that not something that you, yourself, knew as well?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that he was that in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, you're not sure that he was what?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: That he was on the police force at all during 1988.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that is a mistake where reference is made to 1988. Did you mean to say or even did you say 1998, as you said before?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, we're just clarifying one of your answers. You said that you were not sure that Stanisa Radosevic was on the police force at all during a particular year. Were you referring to 1998?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you yourself take part in any military or paramilitary activity during the conflict, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I was only a reservist, but I did not participate in any conflicts. I just stood guard at the Decani police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Along with Mr. Markovic and his brother. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know about his brother. I don't recall his brother being there. And as for Zvonko, I don't remember his having been there either -- in fact, I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just to be clear, when were you called up as a reservist, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. I'm not able to tell you. I was with them for a very short period, perhaps a month or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, we've heard some evidence about the way the reserve police was organised, and correct me if I've got this wrong, but individuals were signed up to be members of the reserve police and then could be called upon for active when required. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So I just want to be clear. When were you first signed up to be a member of the reserve police; that is to say, I'm not asking when you were called up for active duty. When did you first sign up and join the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I was never active, on the active force.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just listen, if you can, and see if you can help us. Were you signed up as a member of the reserve police at the beginning of 1998?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I believe it was in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So on the occasion when you were stopped in Pozhare, Mr. Stijovic, were you already a member of the reserve police then, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the active duty -- sorry, let me rephrase the question. The duty that you were called upon to perform, you say that was limited, was it, to guarding Decan police station?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to put certain allegations to you and give you an opportunity to respond to them, Mr. Stijovic. And for this purpose the registrar who has beside you a bundle of documents can assist you with tab 6, tab 7, tab 10, and tab 11, although these are documents originally written in Albanian and then translated into English. Do you read Albanian?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In that case, let me put the substance of the allegations to you. The first behind tab 6 is a report to the Decan War Crimes Commission by a man called Halil Sadikaj, who describes an incident on the 7th of September, during which the homes of a number of people were looted, and all of the property he describes, including appliances and vehicles, stolen by the police and paramilitaries as part of the September offensive in the area. And amongst those listed as taking part in that operation are Novak Vlahovic, Mika Vlahovic, Goran Vlahovic, Stanisa Radosevic, Novak Stijovic, Zvonko Markovic, Bora Jukic, Ilija Ikic, Moma Ikic, and Moma Stijovic. First of all, is there anyone on that list you don't know personally, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us who you don't know --

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, Ilija Ikic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you don't know Ilija Ikic. Do you know Bora Jukic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness also said Moma Ikic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know Bora Jukic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. So other than those two names, all the other people in that list are people that you know, are they?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Just one second, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It seems to be three names, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, quite right. Your Honour's quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The others are all names that you know apart from Ilija Ikic, Moma Ikic --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I may have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I think apart from those two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct. I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you in Dashinoc in September, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: In Dasinovac, which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In September 1998.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware that your friend Stanisa Radosevic had been present there at a time when remains were recovered belonging to his father?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he told me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where were you in September 1998? Where were you living? Where were you based?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: In Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you in the reserve police by then?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I think that I wasn't. I wasn't definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you working in the factory still, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, the factory had been shut down. So from the day that I was captured, I didn't go to work anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. But it was after that, after that point, you've told us that you joined the police?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I cannot remember exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this: Did you join the police before or after the back pain onset?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It was precisely on that account that I did not remain with the police because I couldn't endure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us in answer to Mr. Di Fazio a few moments ago that your back pain began either three or four or five months after this incident occurred. Are you now saying it was when the back pain began that you stopped being a police officer?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. It was before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, it may be that I misunderstood your testimony. You said a few moments ago when I asked you whether you joined the police before or after the back pain onset. You responded that it was on that account that you did not remain within the police. Can I ask you just to clarify your answer for us for a moment, please. Had the back pain begun before you joined the police, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I had already been feeling pain before that, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand that answer in context with the question, so let me ask you the question again and ask you, if you would, please, for a yes or no answer. Had the back pain begun before you joined the police?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so can you give us an indication at all, please, how long after it began you joined?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I can give you a precise answer. At the time the pain was not strong. It was more occasional pain.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. If we could look with the registrar, please, behind tab 7, there is a report to the Decan War Crimes Commission from someone called Kumrije Sadikaj, who alleges that on the 3rd of April, 1999, in the village of Isniq, police officers were burning houses in the village and stealing from them. And your name is listed amongst others as being part of that police unit. Can we take it that you were in the police, Mr. Stijovic, by the time of April 1999?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, in April I was not in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when exactly did you join the police, then, if it was after April 1999?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that it was later. Actually, it was before, in March -- May, I think it was May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, just for the record, you earlier referred to a document of a humanitarian organisation found under 6, that was D20, Exhibit D20, whereas the document you are now referring to, that is, the statement given to an organisation called the commission for the war crimes, is document 1D00/1704, which still needs a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which has not been marked, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D151, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could turn now to tab 10, please, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a record held by the International Crisis Group, Mr. Stijovic of a report of someone called Pren Gjokaj reporting an incident in Bardhaniq on the 6th of April, 1999, in which it is alleged that police officers, together with the army and paramilitaries in blue and multi-coloured uniforms, equipped with machine-guns, pistols, grenades, knives, and armoured artillery, started to shell the village and forced the villagers to leave. You are listed together with Rade Vlahovic, Ljubisa Radunovic, and others, as having taken part in that operation in Bardhaniq. Now, I think you've just told us that you were by then a police officer. Is that right? The date, I remind you, is the 6th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Never in my life was I involved with Radovic -- Ljubisa Radunovic or Rade Vlahovic. Moreover, I wasn't involved with anyone else either, and as long as I served on the police force at all I just guarded buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
