utterances.text: I see. I want, finally, if I may, to return to the incident that took place on the outskirts of Gllogjan. I'm going to suggest to you that it was clear to you that the reason why you and Stanisa Radosevic were being singled out in that incident was because the people who were assaulting you thought that you were connected with the police. It wasn't based on your ethnicity at all.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was quite the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, very well. Let me just test that with you, if I may, for a moment, please. Because if I have the position correctly from the testimony that you've given and the statements that you've made there were a total of six people of Serbian ethnicity who were detained at the crossroads at Pozhare. I just want to run through it with you, if I may. Of the group that you were with, you've told us, first of all, that Mrs. Radosevic was not ill-treated. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Stanisa Radosevic has given evidence that during the course of this incident one of the men who was present and was holding a sniper rifle during this assault asked him, "Is this your mother?" And when he replied that it was. The man said, "Then she is my mother, too." And he told everybody present to leave her alone. Do you remember one of the men who was there saying that this lady who was clearly a Serb was his mother, too?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't heard of that. All I know is that they singled out -- they were singled out and put on the side. They were not beaten or mistreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your father, you learned, was also stopped at the crossroads at Pozhare, and do I have it correct that he was stopped with two other people of Serbian ethnicity, Milka Stijovic and Stana Popovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Milka Stijovic, she is your sister-in-law. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No. She's the wife of a distant uncle of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. How old is she, roughly? Sorry, may I put that question again. How old was she, roughly, in 1998?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I think she was 55 or 60, perhaps. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Stana Popovic was a neighbour of your families; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And each of those individuals was released without being in any way harmed or assaulted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And although you made mention of your father having his hat knocked off at one point, it's quite right to say that he was never struck, was he, according to him?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, he was not, or yes, he was?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't beat him except for hitting him once when his cap was knocked off he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the question was whether it was right to say that, and then the answer: Yes, of course, is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I was anxious that it may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- have lost some meaning in translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your father was interviewed by the same woman from the humanitarian organisation at the same time and at the same place as you were interviewed, on the 25th of April. Do you remember him being there when you spoke to the lady from that organisation?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, she has testified before the Tribunal that your father told her that he was never hit, that he was re-assured that he and those with him would not be harmed, but that his hat was knocked off his head. Does that broadly reflect what he told you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so of the six people who were stopped at the crossroads, it was you two, yourself and Mr. Stanisa Radosevic, who were picked on?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, do you have any questions for Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, do you have any questions for Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, is there any need to re-examine Mr. Stijovic? MR. DI FAZIO: Just a few matters, if I may, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: It won't take long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You were asked questions about the state of chaos or disorder that you observed when you were stopped, and you were asked if anyone was in charge or whether it was chaotic. Did you observe any chaos or disorder when you were initially being driven from Pozar towards Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I noticed that there was nobody who seemed to be the main man there. Everybody was doing as they saw fit, as they pleased.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did Jusuf do?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: He returned to Pozar village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you were first stopped at Pozar, did -- was there any confusion or chaos about what should be done with you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How was it resolved, if it was?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was resolved that we would go to Glodjane because that's what Jusuf ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Jusuf there when you arrived in Glodjane -- when you first arrived in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but he left straight away and he was the one who drove us to Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When the rifle-butts and the bars, rods, and the boots were being applied to you and Stanisa, was Stanisa's mother present and able to observe this?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: During the course of the beating that you and Stanisa suffered, were there any accusations made to you regarding your membership of the police forces?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You were asked questions by Defence counsel concerning what you reported to a humanitarian law organisation, and part of what you said to them, apparently, was put to you. I want to -- MR. DI FAZIO: And, Madam Registrar, it's the document that is under tab 1 or document 1. I believe it's also P5, if Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: But I can deal with it simply by putting the quote to you. In that document this is what you are alleged to have said. "When we got to the village they made us get out of the car and started beating us. They beat us with bars and kicked and punched us for about half an hour or maybe 40 minutes. Then the questioning started ..." Would you -- is that an accurate reflection of what you told the lady from -- or the person from this humanitarian organisation?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you notice or observe any indecision of chaos about whether or not the beating was to start at that particular point?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think they thought about it for any length of time. They started beating us straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was Jusuf there at the time this attack was launched on you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. In that particular document that I've just asked you questions about, this is what you are alleged to have said to the lady or to the person from the humanitarian organisation, talking about the episode when you were taken and locked in a room with Stanisa's mother. "When he left, they locked me and his mother in a room. Two soldiers were in there with us. They asked if we had relatives on the police force, which we said we didn't. They asked if any of the villagers was a member of the police force. We said none, except for the one they knew about anyway." Does that sound like what you may -- or what you told the person from the humanitarian organisation?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Well, when you said that, who were you referring to when you said: "We said none was a member of the police force except for the one they knew about anyway." Who were you referring to when you said that, the person that they knew about anyway?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Vukicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And is he the police officer from the MUP I think in Decani?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And the lady who -- sorry, the person -- I keep saying "the lady," but do you know anyone named Marijana Andjelkovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: If -- did the person from the humanitarian organisation who interviewed you, was it a woman?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you -- have you got any idea of what that woman's name was?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Marijana Andjelkovic from the Humanitarian Law Centre has testified that she participated in interviewing people, including you. Would -- does that -- any reason to disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I agree, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's get back to what you said to the -- to her, that quote that I just recently read to you. You said, according to the quote that I read to you, that you found yourself in a situation in a room with two soldiers, and those two soldiers asked if you had any relatives on the police force and you said you didn't. And then they asked if any of the villagers were members of the police force. Do you remember that being asked of you inside the room; in other words, if you could tell them -- if you could tell them who was a police officer?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They did not ask me that in the room. They asked us that while we were outside. When we were in the room, there was only one of them with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: But -- okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: And another one came and went, never stayed long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Fine. But what I want to know is this: Did they ask you who was a police officer from your village? Did they want that information from you?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Not when we were in the room. That was outside, and I don't know who it was who asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if I might just ask one supplementary rising out of that line of questioning relating to this document. It won't take a second or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to be clear, Mr. Stijovic, you said those questions were being asked whilst you were outside, that is to say before you were in the room. Stanisa Radosevic had gone by the time you were in the room, had he not?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it right to say those questions about the police generally and about who had been responsible for the shooting of Albanians on the 24th of March, they were being asked at the time that you were being assaulted outside in the street?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic, I would have one or two questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said the house you were taken where you stayed in a room for one hour, one hour and a half, was a private house. Were there many people in this house or were there just, as you would find normally in a private house, a couple of persons like parents, children, perhaps grandparents, or were there perhaps more people in that house than you would expect to find in a private house?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone inside the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it a large house?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I think it has two storeys.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you said: "I didn't see anyone inside the house," you were kept there with someone next to you. Did you mean to say, I saw no one in the house, to say that you didn't see what you would expect to be ordinary inhabitants of that house?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, is there anything you observed which would lead you to believe that this house was taken at random or not taken at random to be brought to?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I was in that one room and it had a metal door and bars on the windows, and you access that room straight from outdoors. You don't go through the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did anyone say anything about where you went? Was it the first house? Was it three houses from where the car broke down? Is there any clue you could give us as to why specifically this house was chosen to take you to?

utterances.speaker: NOVAK STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Stijovic, this concludes your testimony in this court, at least if I may assume that the questions put by the Bench have not triggered any need for further questions by the parties. Mr. Stijovic, I would like to thank you very much for coming to Pristina and to answer the questions put to you by the parties and the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can conclude the videolink. Thank you, Madam Registrar in Pristina, for assisting us. The parties were informed earlier that they were invited for a meeting in Chambers. That meeting that was supposed to take place in room M-177 is no longer necessary at this moment and therefore is postponed or perhaps even cancelled forever. This is just to inform the parties about this. Then it is very tempting to try to find additional time to do procedural matters at this moment. The Chamber, however, even if such time would be found gives priority to other matters. Therefore, unless there's anything of great urgency, we'll adjourn until the 20th of August. I do not see any such urgent procedural matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Nothing urgent, but I will, if I may, after we rise invite Madam Registrar to assign an identification number in respect of one document in the bundle that was referred to but not -- does not yet have an identification mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then I think D151, is there any objection against admission, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: On the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the contrary. So then D151 is admitted into evidence. Perhaps we can deal with the other document right away to assign a number to it have a number assigned. I ask the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That would be document number 10, the ICG report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the ICG report. Madam Registrar, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is will be Exhibit Number D152, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, any objection against D152? MR. DI FAZIO: No, none, Your Honour, and none to any of the documents that were questioned about and put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that all the others were in evidence already if I'm not mistaken, but this means that D152 now is in, admitted into evidence as well. We'll not see each other for quite a couple of weeks. To the extent that you'll be in a position to find some relaxation from what happens in this court - and I know that that's not available at least for some of us - I wish you all the best until the 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've forgotten to tell that the 20th of August will be quarter past 2.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of August, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
